rationale: The capex-minus-own-5-year-mean leg is essentially Titman-Wei-Xie abnormal capital investment, and the whole construct is a cosmetic recoding (TS_RANK → deviation-from-moving-average) of the archive's "Own-History Capex-Profit Mismatch" rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Beyond being a level-to-change swap on the second leg of "Liquidity-Supported Maintenance Alignment," the conditioning variable is internally problematic: NEG(DELTA(lct/act)) high means net working capital is expanding, i.e. high working-capital accruals, which the accrual anomaly says predicts *lower* returns and thus fights the stated positive sign.

The liquidity-to-intangible composition shift is a genuinely different construct from the archive's intangible tests (no leverage screen, no lagged cash-flow gate), though it subtracts two differently-scaled deltas (÷at vs ÷act) and risks being mostly a mechanical cash-financed-acquisition/asset-growth proxy.

Replacing the operating-cash-flow coverage leg with a within-firm-demeaned cash stock is a substantive (not cosmetic) change to the archive's best inventory signal, plausibly improving coverage and reducing profitability contamination, but it remains close enough to "Inventory-Cash Coverage Imbalance" that any result must be shown to be incremental to it.

NEG(ABS(delta capex − delta sales intensity)) is maximized when both changes are near zero, so the signal mostly proxies for corporate inaction/low fundamental volatility rather than deliberate "alignment," and the MIN-with-NEG(lct/act) wrapper repeats the structure already tested in "Liquidity-Supported Maintenance Alignment."

capx − Δ(accumulated depreciation) is just net fixed investment, so this reduces to the well-documented investment/asset-growth anomaly interacted with a financial-constraint proxy (Li–Zhang, Lipson–Mortal–Schill), and it also asserts the mirror-image sign of the archive's "Cash-Constrained Replacement Shortfall" without explaining why both excess and shortfall should predict low returns.
